policy.description: Blocking line-coverage ratchets. Update measured counts in the same reviewed change whenever scope or coverage advances; never lower a floor without an explicit, justified scope change.

tolerance.rationale: The #369 body-observer ownership fix adds one instrumented and covered client/core line so stale handles compare their exact subscriber identity before cleanup, advancing the reviewed high-water from 2326/2666 (87.247%) to 2327/2667 (87.252%). Two clean Node 22.20/V8 runs on 2026-07-27 each passed all 1788 tests across 233 files and reproduced exactly 2327/2667. Retaining the existing one-line tolerance makes the minimum 2326/2667 (87.214%), stricter than the prior 2325/2666 tolerated floor (87.209%). coverage-baseline.test.js retains the exact below-floor, above-baseline, scope-change, and broad-tolerance negative boundaries.

EP-01.3 (#506) adds kernel-owned request bounds and their structured 413: PlatformRequestBounds with the five independently-bounded axes and its Utf8JsonReader scanner, PlatformBoundBreach, and the PlatformBoundedBodyFilter resource filter, moving the instrumented scope from 36,405 to 36,489 lines. Every added line is exercised. PlatformRequestBoundsTests checks each axis at the limit and at the limit plus one, because a bound only ever tested far from its edge does not say where the edge is; it also pins the three scanner invariants that are easy to get wrong and silent when wrong - sibling containers must not share a count, a nested container is charged to its parent rather than to itself, and a property value must not be counted as an array element on top of its key. String length is asserted in UTF-8 bytes rather than characters, since counting characters would admit a body three times the intended size. Malformed JSON is asserted NOT to be reported as a bounds breach, so a consumer that sent nonsense is not told to send less. PlatformBoundedBodyFilterTests covers the declared-length refusal, the chunked body that declares no length at all, the buffered hand-off that model binding depends on, and the fact that the refusal carries a correlation id in both body and header even though it fires before the filter that normally assigns one. Two off-by-ones were found by these tests during development rather than in review: Utf8JsonReader's CurrentDepth counts enclosing containers and so runs one below the nesting level, and the test's own multi-byte fixture used a two-byte character where it needed three. Nine clean .NET 10.0.9/Coverlet runs on 2026-07-29 each passed all 2,410 tests at the same 36,489-line scope and measured 27,767 covered lines five times, 27,763 twice, and 27,769 and 27,768 once each, so the reviewed high-water is 27,769 (76.102%) over an observed Coverlet spread of six lines. The tolerance moves from five lines to six to match that measured spread exactly, because a five-line tolerance would put the floor at 27,764 and reject the 27,763 runs observed here on unchanged code; it is widened by measurement, not to absorb a failure. The floor still rises to 27,763/36,489 (76.086%) from the prior 27,684/36,405 (76.039%), so the ratchet tightens in percentage terms. coverage-baseline.test.js retains the exact scope-drift, regression, stale-baseline, and broad-tolerance negative boundaries.
